cohort: The study included 201,566 weighted samples from Demographic and Health Survey datasets across 25 Sub-Saharan African countries.
finding: The pooled prevalence of perinatal mortality in Sub-Saharan Africa was 46.63 per 1000 total births, with significant spatial clustering, and was predicted by no antenatal care, short birth intervals, cesarean section delivery, unemployment, and households without children.
mod_finding: Women undergoing cesarean section delivery were identified as a significant spatial predictor of perinatal mortality.
country: Sub-Saharan Africa (25 countries including Nigeria, Madagascar, Rwanda, Malawi, Burundi, Gambia, Uganda, Cote d'Ivoire, Angola, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso, Senegal, Kenya, Gabon, South Africa, Ghana, Mali, Mauritania)
cross-section timing: Data collected from Demographic and Health Survey datasets between 2015 and 2023.
